[**Model Context Protocol (MCP**](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction)**)** is a popular open standard from Anthropic that provides AI **models** (usually LLMs) with **context**: resources, tools, etc. MCP operates effectively within the bounds of a "single agent", since it enables the connection between the LLM and its tools/resources.

legacy_root.question: Do the competing agent-interoperability protocols (A2A-class, agent-connect-class) expose any capability MCP cannot express, and is the marginal capability worth a second adapter — or is the honest answer that supporting one protocol well beats supporting two badly?

receipt.line: SUCCESS:RES-0045 in the receipt AND a per-protocol unique-capability list (possibly empty and explicitly marked so) plus a reasoned adopt/decline recommendation

recommendation.capability_lost_by_declining: Native A2A Agent Card federation, A2A CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig webhooks, and agent-connect REST run/thread wait-cancel without a bridge.
recommendation.capability_lost_if_declined: Native A2A Agent Card federation, A2A CreateTaskPushNotificationConfig webhooks, and agent-connect REST run/thread wait-cancel (/runs/{run_id}/wait, /threads/{thread_id}, /agents/{agent_id}/descriptor) without a bridge.
recommendation.rationale: A2A-class and agent-connect-class do expose first-class objects MCP does not (C1, C2). Those objects are the agent-to-agent layer; MCP is the agent-to-tool layer (A2A's own comparison page). This program already needs MCP unique methods (C3). A second adapter without current A2A/ACP peers doubles breakage surface for a capability this estate does not yet call. Honest answer: NO — support MCP well; bridge if a peer appears.
recommendation.reason: Complementary layers, not replacements. One well-supported MCP adapter beats two half-supported agent-protocol adapters.
